tasks.name: Install floor protection at wainscot work zone
tasks.notes: Canvas drop cloth runners along base of wainscot work area. Wainscot is low to floor — drip protection from brush/spray and sanding dust is the primary concern.

tasks.name: Mask wall above cap rail line
tasks.notes: Paper + tape masking above cap rail to protect wall from overspray. Spray only — brush application typically needs no wall masking. 12-inch masking paper adequate for overspray drift at wainscot height.

sop_modules.name: Surface Preparation
sop_modules.notes: Prep tasks vary by substrate type and state. Caulk after fill/sand, before primer. MDF edge seal is mandatory for bare MDF — separate task before latex primer.

tasks.name: Dust and clean all wainscot surfaces
tasks.notes: Remove construction dust, debris, and surface contamination from all wainscot components. Tack cloth or damp wipe. First prep step.

tasks.name: Sand wainscot per substrate and state
tasks.notes: Bare MDF: 220 grit faces. Bare FJP/softwood: 150-180 grit. Bare hardwood: 150-220 grit. Factory-primed (SS_PRIMED_FACTORY): scuff sand 150-180 grit for adhesion. Panels, rails, stiles — all surfaces.

tasks.name: Fill fastener holes and minor defects
tasks.notes: Fill nail/brad holes on panels and frame members. QT3: fill obvious holes. QT4: fill all visible holes. QT5: fill every hole regardless of size, check with raking light.

tasks.name: Sand filled areas smooth
tasks.notes: Sand all filled areas flush with 220 grit. QT5: check with raking light for uniformity. Rigid sanding block for flat panels (FFD §15.4.1).

tasks.name: Caulk panel-to-frame internal joints
tasks.notes: Paintable acrylic latex caulk at: (1) panel-to-rail joints (horizontal), (2) panel-to-stile joints (vertical). Internal joint density varies by wainscot_type — raised_panel has more joints than flat_panel. Caulk quantity scales with assembly SF.

tasks.name: Caulk wainscot-to-wall junction
tasks.notes: Paintable acrylic latex caulk at wainscot assembly perimeter where it meets drywall. Continuous bead along top and sides where wainscot abuts wall. LF proportional to wainscot SF installed.

sop_modules.name: Primer Application
sop_modules.notes: CONDITIONAL — only runs when substrate_state = SS_BARE. Factory-primed (SS_PRIMED_FACTORY) substrates skip this module entirely. Primer type driven by substrate: MDF=SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX (after edge seal), FJP=SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK, hardwood=SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK, softwood=SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC.

tasks.name: Prime wainscot panel assembly
tasks.notes: Full primer coat on all wainscot surfaces. Spray: broad passes on panels, detail on frame profiles. Brush: work systematically panel by panel. MDF: this is step 2 of two-step prime (edges already sealed). Thin coat on raised panel profiles — avoid buildup in recesses.

tasks.name: Light sand primer for finish coat adhesion
tasks.notes: 220 grit light sand entire primed surface. Provides tooth for finish coat. Tack cloth after sanding.

sop_modules.name: Finish Coat Application
sop_modules.notes: Finish coat on all wainscot surfaces. Material system QT-driven: QT3=SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4=SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5=SYS_FF_PREMIUM. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1).

tasks.name: Spray finish coat on wainscot
tasks.notes: Spray technique: field panels first (broad passes), then frame detail (HVLP or fine-finish tip). Beadboard: thin passes to preserve groove definition. Raised panel: ensure full coverage in recessed profiles. Wall masking must be in place above cap rail.

tasks.name: Brush finish coat on wainscot
tasks.notes: Work panel by panel, then frame members. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD §15.3.1). Flat panels: Roll and Tip methodology (FFD §15.6) for even coverage. Raised panel: brush sized to profile. Beadboard: work with groove direction, avoid buildup.

sop_modules.name: Between-Coat Interstage
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat
sop_modules.notes: Universal at ALL quality tiers. Sanding discipline varies by QT: QT3=spot sand only (nibs, rough spots), QT4=full 220 grit, QT5=thorough 220-320 grit. Rigid sanding block mandatory for defect removal (FFD §15.4.1).

tasks.name: Clean work area between coats
tasks.notes: Remove dust, debris from floor protection and work area. Ensure clean environment for next coat.

tasks.name: Inspect previous coat
tasks.notes: QT3: quick glance at 6ft — obvious defects only. QT4: systematic scan at 3ft — all visible defects marked. QT5: lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance. Check panel-to-frame junctions for holidays (especially raised_panel).

tasks.name: Sand between coats
tasks.notes: QT3: spot sand nibs/rough spots only. QT4: full 220 grit entire surface. QT5: thorough 220-320 grit, uniform scratch pattern. Rigid sanding block mandatory on flat panels (FFD §15.4.1). Flexible sanding sponge acceptable for beadboard grooves and raised panel profiles.

tasks.name: Patch and repair marked defects
tasks.notes: Fill, sand, and spot-prime any defects found during inspection. Scope varies by QT.

tasks.name: Spot coat patched areas
tasks.notes: Touch-up patched areas to match surrounding finish before next full coat.

tasks.name: Tack cloth all wainscot surfaces
tasks.notes: Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth before next coat application. Cover every SF of wainscot surface.

tasks.name: Final quality inspection
tasks.notes: QT3: scan for obvious defects at 6ft. QT4: systematic review at 3ft of all surfaces. QT5: critical lighted inspection at arm's length. Key checkpoints: panel-to-frame junction holidays, brush marks on flat panels, groove definition on beadboard, caulk line quality, overall sheen uniformity.

tasks.name: Touch-up defects found during final inspection
tasks.notes: Correct any remaining defects. Feather touch-ups into surrounding finish. QT5: may require full additional coat if defects are widespread.

tasks.name: Remove wall masking
tasks.notes: Score tape edge before removal. Pull at 45-degree angle to prevent wall damage or paint peel.

tasks.name: Remove floor protection
tasks.notes: Remove canvas drop cloths from wainscot base perimeter. Fold inward to contain debris.

tasks.name: Vacuum work area
tasks.notes: Vacuum floor area after protection removal. Remove sanding dust and debris.

tasks.name: Clean tools and equipment
tasks.notes: Clean brushes, spray equipment, dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne products. Solvent cleanup for shellac-based MDF edge sealer residue.

workflow_sequence.standard_bare: MOD_WNSC_SETUP → MOD_WNSC_PREP → MOD_WNSC_PRIME → MOD_WNSC_INTERSTAGE → MOD_WNSC_FINISH_COAT(1) → MOD_WNSC_INTERSTAGE → MOD_WNSC_FINISH_COAT(2) → MOD_WNSC_FINAL_INSPECT → MOD_WNSC_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.standard_factory_primed: MOD_WNSC_SETUP → MOD_WNSC_PREP → MOD_WNSC_FINISH_COAT(1) → MOD_WNSC_INTERSTAGE → MOD_WNSC_FINISH_COAT(2) → MOD_WNSC_FINAL_INSPECT → MOD_WNSC_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.qt5_brush: MOD_WNSC_SETUP → MOD_WNSC_PREP → [MOD_WNSC_PRIME] → [MOD_WNSC_INTERSTAGE] → MOD_WNSC_FINISH_COAT(1) → MOD_WNSC_INTERSTAGE → MOD_WNSC_FINISH_COAT(2) → MOD_WNSC_INTERSTAGE → MOD_WNSC_FINISH_COAT(3) → MOD_WNSC_FINAL_INSPECT → MOD_WNSC_CLEANUP
workflow_sequence.notes: Prime module conditional on substrate_state = SS_BARE. QT5 brush adds additional FINISH_COAT + INTERSTAGE cycle per FFD §15.10.3. Single paintable item (ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL, SF) — no internal component sequencing needed.
